next_step.guide: Give the oldest the reading-and-teaching part and the youngest two the touch-and-do part at the same time, with a hands-on reset between each short burst.
next_step.learner: The oldest reads one fact aloud and shows the youngest; the youngest two find or touch the thing outside and say what they notice.

reach.alone: The oldest reads a short passage and explains it; the youngest two observe and describe what they see and feel outside.
reach.with_help: The oldest teaches a fact to the youngest and the youngest act it out, with the guide setting the turns so no one waits or drifts.
reach.not_yet: The youngest holding a multi-step written task alone, or the oldest sustaining the group without the guide's turn-setting; keep both for later.

signals.looks_like: wandering off, poking at something unrelated, going quiet during the reading part
signals.not: not an attention problem; it is a sign the reading part ran longer than a young learner's burst

then.detail: The guide triggers the hands-on reset so the youngest has something to touch again.

signals.watch: the oldest stalling while the youngest catch up
signals.looks_like: finished and idle, drifting or taking over the youngest's task
signals.not: not boredom to scold; it is the oldest having outrun the shared pace

then.detail: Offer the oldest a teach-it-forward step so the wait becomes teaching, never a label about patience.

signals.watch: the oldest teaching a fact that lands
signals.looks_like: the youngest repeat or act out what the oldest just showed them
signals.not: not a ranking of the children; it is the swinging-lead working for this group right now

then.detail: Note the teach-forward that worked so the guide can reuse that shape next burst.

companion_may.offer: Suggest the next short burst and the hands-on reset that fits it, split into a read-and-teach part and a touch-and-do part.
companion_may.when: a burst ends or the youngest start to drift
companion_may.ceiling: Suggest the shape; never assign a child to a task or decide who is ready for what.

companion_may.offer: Give the oldest a teach-it-forward prompt when they finish ahead.
companion_may.when: the oldest is waiting with nothing to do
companion_may.ceiling: Offer the prompt; whether the oldest teaches or rests is the guide's and the child's call.

guide_only.reserved: Reading the group's dynamic — who needs the next turn, who is about to drift — and setting the turns.
guide_only.why: The pace of a mixed-age group lives in faces and bodies in the yard, which only the guide sees.

guide_only.reserved: Matching each part to the child in front of them rather than to an age.
guide_only.why: Which child can do what today is a judgement the guide makes, not a split a companion can assume.

guide_only.reserved: Deciding when the whole group has had enough and ending the lesson.
guide_only.why: One lesson for three children ends when the guide sees it should, not on a shared clock.

techniques.move: Split each burst into a read-and-teach part for the oldest and a touch-and-do part for the youngest, with a short hands-on reset between, so the oldest's waiting becomes teaching and the youngest always have something to touch.
techniques.concept: keeping mixed ages engaged in one science lesson together
techniques.stuck_signature: the oldest finishes and waits while the youngest drift during the reading part

services.for: letting the youngest hear a fact when the oldest is busy with their own part
services.boundary: Read only short passages the guide chose; never lead the children or invite them to talk to it.
services.offline_fallback: The oldest reads aloud to the youngest, which is the point of the lesson anyway.

services.for: suggesting a backyard creature or plant that is actually local, so examples are real where the family is
services.boundary: Return a capability-level suggestion to the guide; never geolocate the family or store where they are.

bundle.does: Carries one shared lesson split into bursts with resets, and the next-step pair; the guide runs it in the yard and the game records what the group did.
bundle.cannot: Cannot see the youngest drift or the oldest wait in real time, cannot match a part to the child in front of the guide, and cannot read when the whole group is done — all of that is the guide's.

continuous.unlocks: Noticing drift or waiting as it starts and offering the next burst or a teach-forward step in the moment; across days, following each child's own reach instead of one shared level.
continuous.still_guide_only: Reading the group dynamic and setting the turns stay with the guide, however connected the companion is — this is the sharpest thing only a person can do here.

record_hooks.writes: what the group did in the burst and whether the youngest stayed with it, as behaviour

record_hooks.on: the oldest teaches a fact the youngest act out
record_hooks.writes: that a teach-forward landed, as a confidence signal for the group, not a ranking
a short summary of which parts held the group and where it frayed, in the guide's words
